# Snippets

Short pieces to copy into a program, one per feature. Each is a whole file (or a spec and body pair) that
compiles as it is, in a crate made by `alr init` (`examples/snippets/generate.sh` compiles every one before it
writes this page). The web ones are packages with a `Register` procedure, so they plug into the hello world of
[GETTING_STARTED.md](GETTING_STARTED.md):

```ada
Greetings.Register (Routes);   --  before Servers.Run
```

A handler is a procedure `(Request : Http_Request; Response : in out Http_Response)` declared in a package,
not inside a subprogram, so that its `'Access` can be kept by the router. Each crate's README has the details.

## Routes, parameters and queries

Needs `sparrow_http`.

```ada
--  greetings.ads
with Sparrow.Http.Routers; use Sparrow.Http.Routers;

package Greetings is
   procedure Register (Routes : in out Router);
end Greetings;

--  greetings.adb
with Sparrow; use Sparrow;
with Sparrow.Http; use Sparrow.Http;
with Sparrow.Http.Requests; use Sparrow.Http.Requests;
with Sparrow.Http.Responses;

package body Greetings is

   --  GET /hello/ada?greeting=Hi  ->  "Hi, ada!"
   procedure Greet
     (Request : Http_Request; Response : in out Http_Response)
   is
      Name     : constant UTF8_String := Parameter_Text (Request, "name");
      Greeting : constant UTF8_String :=
        Query_Text (Request, "greeting", Default => "Hello");
   begin
      Responses.Send (Response, OK, Greeting & ", " & Name & "!");
   end Greet;

   --  GET /items/42  ->  "item 42", or 404 for anything but a number
   procedure Show_Item
     (Request : Http_Request; Response : in out Http_Response)
   is
      Id : constant Long_Long_Integer :=
        Integer_Parameter (Request, "id", Default => -1);
   begin
      if Id < 1 then
         Responses.Fail (Response, Not_Found);
      else
         Responses.Send (Response, OK, "item" & UTF8_String (Id'Image));
      end if;
   end Show_Item;

   procedure Register (Routes : in out Router) is
   begin
      Add (Routes, Get, "/hello/:name", Greet'Access);
      --  On_Reactor: it never blocks, so it need not wait for a worker
      Add (Routes, Get, "/items/:id", Show_Item'Access, Run => On_Reactor);
   end Register;

end Greetings;
```

`Parameter_Text`, `Query_Text` and `Form_Text` check that the value is UTF-8 and return text; `Parameter`,
`Query_Value` and `Form_Value` return the raw bytes. A `*name` segment (`/files/*path`) takes the rest of the
path.

## A JSON API

Needs `sparrow_http` (which brings `sparrow_json`).

```ada
--  bookmarks.ads
with Sparrow.Http.Routers; use Sparrow.Http.Routers;

package Bookmarks is
   procedure Register (Routes : in out Router);
end Bookmarks;

--  bookmarks.adb
with Sparrow; use Sparrow;
with Sparrow.Http; use Sparrow.Http;
with Sparrow.Http.Requests;
with Sparrow.Http.Responses;
with Sparrow.Json; use Sparrow.Json;
with Sparrow.Json.Builders;

package body Bookmarks is

   Rules : constant Rule_List :=
     [Required ("url", Text_Shape, Shortest => 1, Longest => 2048),
      Optional ("title", Text_Shape, Longest => 200)];

   --  POST /bookmarks  {"url": "https://ada-lang.io", "title": "Ada"}
   procedure Create
     (Request : Http_Request; Response : in out Http_Response)
   is
      Fields : constant Document := Requests.Json_Body (Request);
      Reply  : Builders.Builder (Response.Content'Access);
   begin
      if not Is_Valid (Fields) then
         Responses.Send (Response, Bad_Request, "the body is not JSON");
         return;
      elsif Problem (Fields, Rules) /= "" then
         --  "url: required", "title: too long", ...
         Responses.Send
           (Response, Unprocessable_Content, Problem (Fields, Rules));
         return;
      end if;

      --  ... store it ...

      Responses.Begin_Content (Response, Created, Application_Json);
      Reply.Begin_Object;
      Reply.Member ("url", Text (Fields, "url"));
      Reply.Member ("title", Text (Fields, "title"));
      Reply.Key ("tags");
      Reply.Begin_Array;
      Reply.Value ("ada");
      Reply.End_Array;
      Reply.End_Object;   --  {"url":"...","title":"Ada","tags":["ada"]}
   end Create;

   procedure Register (Routes : in out Router) is
   begin
      Add (Routes, Post, "/bookmarks", Create'Access);
   end Register;

end Bookmarks;
```

Reading nested values: `Integer_Value (Doc, "page.count", Default => 1)`, `Text (Doc, "items.0.title")`, and
`for Item in Json.Iteration.Elements (Doc, "items") loop ... Text (Doc, "title", From => Item) ...`.

## Static files

Needs `sparrow_http`.

```ada
--  site.ads
with Sparrow.Http.Routers; use Sparrow.Http.Routers;

package Site is
   procedure Register (Routes : in out Router);
end Site;

--  site.adb
with Sparrow.Http; use Sparrow.Http;
with Sparrow.Http.Static;

package body Site is

   procedure Register (Routes : in out Router) is
   begin
      --  public/index.html at /, public/css/app.css at /css/app.css.
      --  Other routes still win over this one.
      Add (Routes, Get, "/*file", Static.Folder ("public", Max_Age => 3600));
   end Register;

end Site;
```

`ETag`, 304, byte ranges (video seeking, resumed downloads), gzip and `app.js.gz` siblings come with it.
Paths that climb out of the folder are refused.

## HTTPS and HTTP/2

Needs `sparrow_http`. A certificate for local work:
`openssl req -x509 -newkey ec -pkeyopt ec_paramgen_curve:P-256 -nodes -days 30 -subj /CN=localhost -keyout key.pem -out cert.pem`.

```ada
--  secure_hello.adb
with Greetings;
with Sparrow.Http; use Sparrow.Http;
with Sparrow.Http.Routers; use Sparrow.Http.Routers;
with Sparrow.Http.Servers;
with Sparrow.Tls;

procedure Secure_Hello is
   Routes      : Router (Capacity => 8);
   Certificate : aliased Sparrow.Tls.Context;
begin
   Sparrow.Tls.Open_Server (Certificate, "cert.pem", "key.pem");
   if not Sparrow.Tls.Is_Open (Certificate) then
      raise Program_Error with Sparrow.Tls.Last_Failure (Certificate);
   end if;

   Greetings.Register (Routes);
   Servers.Run
     (Servers.From_Environment, Routes, Security => Certificate'Access);
end Secure_Hello;
```

Browsers pick HTTP/2 on their own; handlers do not change. `curl -k --http2 https://localhost:8080/hello/you`.

## Passwords

Needs `sparrow_crypto`. Argon2id, with the salt and cost kept in the stored string.

```ada
--  password_hashes.ads
package Password_Hashes is
   function New_Hash (Password : String) return String;   --  store this
   function Matches (Password, Stored : String) return Boolean;
end Password_Hashes;

--  password_hashes.adb
with Sparrow.Crypto.Passwords; use Sparrow.Crypto;
with Sparrow.Crypto.Random;

package body Password_Hashes is

   function New_Hash (Password : String) return String is
      Salt : Passwords.Salt_Bytes;
   begin
      Random.Fill (Salt);
      --  "$argon2id$v=19$m=19456,t=2,p=1$<salt>$<hash>"
      return Passwords.Hash (Password, Salt);
   end New_Hash;

   --  Compared in constant time.
   function Matches (Password, Stored : String) return Boolean is
     (Passwords.Verify (Password, Stored));

end Password_Hashes;
```

Hashing takes tens of milliseconds by design: do it in handlers on workers (the default). After a successful
login, `Passwords.Needs_Rehash (Stored)` says when to store a fresh hash.

## Sessions, login and CSRF

Needs `sparrow_http`. The session is sealed into a cookie (AES-256-GCM); the server keeps nothing.

```ada
--  accounts.ads
with Sparrow.Http.Routers; use Sparrow.Http.Routers;

package Accounts is
   procedure Register (Routes : in out Router);
end Accounts;

--  accounts.adb
with Sparrow; use Sparrow;
with Sparrow.Http; use Sparrow.Http;
with Sparrow.Http.Requests; use Sparrow.Http.Requests;
with Sparrow.Http.Responses;
with Sparrow.Http.Sessions; use Sparrow.Http.Sessions;
with Sparrow.IO.Process;

package body Accounts is

   --  SESSION_SECRET: 32 random bytes or more (openssl rand -base64 48).
   --  Without it, sessions last until the program restarts.
   Visitors : constant Store :=
     Cookie_Store
       (Secret => Sparrow.IO.Process.Environment
                    ("SESSION_SECRET", Default => Random_Secret));

   --  Look the user up in your database, and check with Password_Hashes.
   function Password_Is_Right (Email, Password : String) return Boolean is
     (Email /= "" and then Password /= "");

   procedure Show_Login
     (Request : Http_Request; Response : in out Http_Response)
   is
      Session : Sessions.Session := Visitors.Load (Request);
   begin
      Responses.Send
        (Response, OK,
         "<form method=post action=/login>"
         & UTF8_String (Csrf_Field (Session))
         & "<input name=email> <input name=password type=password>"
         & "<button>Log in</button></form>",
         Media_Type => Text_Html);
      Visitors.Save (Session, Response);   --  the cookie, when it changed
   end Show_Login;

   procedure Log_In
     (Request : Http_Request; Response : in out Http_Response)
   is
      Session : Sessions.Session := Visitors.Load (Request);
   begin
      if not Csrf_Valid (Session, Request) then
         Responses.Fail (Response, Forbidden);
         return;
      end if;
      if not Password_Is_Right
               (Form_Value (Request, "email"), Form_Value (Request, "password"))
      then
         Responses.Redirect (Response, "/login");
         return;
      end if;
      Renew (Session);   --  a new CSRF token at every login
      Set (Session, "user", Form_Text (Request, "email"));
      Visitors.Save (Session, Response);
      Responses.Redirect (Response, "/me");
   end Log_In;

   procedure Show_Me
     (Request : Http_Request; Response : in out Http_Response)
   is
      Session : constant Sessions.Session := Visitors.Load (Request);
   begin
      if Has (Session, "user") then
         Responses.Send
           (Response, OK, "Signed in as " & Get (Session, "user"));
      else
         Responses.Redirect (Response, "/login");
      end if;
   end Show_Me;

   procedure Log_Out
     (Request : Http_Request; Response : in out Http_Response)
   is
      Session : Sessions.Session := Visitors.Load (Request);
   begin
      if Csrf_Valid (Session, Request) then
         Clear (Session);
         Visitors.Save (Session, Response);
      end if;
      Responses.Redirect (Response, "/login");
   end Log_Out;

   procedure Register (Routes : in out Router) is
   begin
      Add (Routes, Get, "/login", Show_Login'Access);
      Add (Routes, Post, "/login", Log_In'Access);
      Add (Routes, Get, "/me", Show_Me'Access);
      Add (Routes, Post, "/logout", Log_Out'Access);
   end Register;

end Accounts;
```

Scripts send the token in an `X-CSRF-Token` header instead (`Sessions.Csrf_Token (Session)`). To keep sessions
on the server, use `Sessions.Table_Store` with a `Session_Table` (see the Valkey snippet).

## Bearer tokens (JWT)

Needs `sparrow_jwt`. HS256 with a shared secret; `Sparrow.Jwt.Key_Sets` verifies RS256, ES256 and EdDSA
tokens against another service's JWKS.

```ada
--  api_tokens.ads
with Sparrow.Http.Routers; use Sparrow.Http.Routers;

package Api_Tokens is
   procedure Register (Routes : in out Router);
end Api_Tokens;

--  api_tokens.adb
with Sparrow; use Sparrow;
with Sparrow.Http; use Sparrow.Http;
with Sparrow.Http.Requests; use Sparrow.Http.Requests;
with Sparrow.Http.Responses;
with Sparrow.IO.Process;
with Sparrow.Json;
with Sparrow.Jwt;

package body Api_Tokens is

   --  JWT_SECRET: 32 random bytes or more.
   Signing : constant Jwt.Key :=
     Jwt.To_Key (Sparrow.IO.Process.Environment ("JWT_SECRET"));

   --  POST /token. In real life, after checking a password.
   procedure Issue
     (Request : Http_Request; Response : in out Http_Response)
   is
      Token : constant String :=
        Jwt.Sign_Subject
          (Signing, Subject => "user-42", Now => Now (Request),
           Lifetime => 3600);
   begin
      Responses.Send (Response, OK, UTF8_String (Token));   --  JWTs are ASCII
   end Issue;

   --  GET /private with "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
   procedure Private_Page
     (Request : Http_Request; Response : in out Http_Response)
   is
      Token  : constant String :=
        Jwt.Bearer_Token (Header (Request, "Authorization"));
      Claims : Json.Document (Node_Capacity => 64, Text_Capacity => 4096);
      Valid  : Boolean;
   begin
      Jwt.Verify (Signing, Token, Now (Request), Claims, Valid);
      if not Valid then
         Responses.Set_Header (Response, "WWW-Authenticate", "Bearer");
         Responses.Fail (Response, Unauthorized);
         return;
      end if;
      Responses.Send (Response, OK, "Hello, " & Json.Text (Claims, "sub"));
   end Private_Page;

   procedure Register (Routes : in out Router) is
   begin
      Add (Routes, Post, "/token", Issue'Access);
      Add (Routes, Get, "/private", Private_Page'Access);
   end Register;

end Api_Tokens;
```

## SQLite, one connection per worker

Needs `sparrow_sqlite`. Each worker task opens its own connection at start: no pool, no locks.

```ada
--  todo_store.ads
with Sparrow.Http.Routers; use Sparrow.Http.Routers;
with Sparrow.Http.Servers;

package Todo_Store is
   procedure Register (Routes : in out Router);

   --  Pass to Servers.Run: each worker opens its connection as it starts.
   function Hooks return Sparrow.Http.Servers.Worker_Hooks;
end Todo_Store;

--  todo_store.adb
with Sparrow.Http; use Sparrow.Http;
with Sparrow.Http.Requests; use Sparrow.Http.Requests;
with Sparrow.Http.Responses;
with Sparrow.Json.Builders;
with Sparrow.Sqlite; use Sparrow.Sqlite;
with Sparrow.Sqlite.Migrations;
with Sparrow.Sqlite.Per_Worker;

package body Todo_Store is

   --  One step per change. Add steps; never edit one that has run.
   Steps : constant Migrations.Step_List :=
     [Migrations.Step
        (1, "CREATE TABLE todos (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT)"),
      Migrations.Step
        (2, "ALTER TABLE todos ADD COLUMN done INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0")];

   package Databases is new Sparrow.Sqlite.Per_Worker
     (Worker_Id, Path => "todos.db", Steps => Steps);

   function Hooks return Sparrow.Http.Servers.Worker_Hooks is
     (On_Start => Databases.Open'Access, On_Stop => Databases.Close'Access);

   --  GET /todos  ->  [{"id":1,"title":"Write Ada","done":false}]
   procedure List
     (Request : Http_Request; Response : in out Http_Response)
   is
      Db    : Database renames Databases.Connection (Worker (Request));
      Find  : Statement;
      Reply : Sparrow.Json.Builders.Builder (Response.Content'Access);
   begin
      Prepare (Db, Find, "SELECT id, title, done FROM todos");
      Responses.Begin_Content (Response, OK, Application_Json);
      Reply.Begin_Array;
      for Row in Rows (Find) loop
         Reply.Begin_Object;
         Reply.Member ("id", Row.Integer_Value ("id"));
         Reply.Member ("title", Row.Text ("title"));
         Reply.Member ("done", Row.Integer_Value ("done") /= 0);
         Reply.End_Object;
      end loop;
      Reply.End_Array;
   end List;

   --  POST /todos with a form field "title"
   procedure Add_Todo
     (Request : Http_Request; Response : in out Http_Response)
   is
      Db     : Database renames Databases.Connection (Worker (Request));
      Insert : Statement;
   begin
      Prepare (Db, Insert, "INSERT INTO todos (title) VALUES (?1)");
      Bind (Insert, 1, Form_Text (Request, "title"));
      Run (Insert);
      Responses.Redirect (Response, "/todos");
   end Add_Todo;

   procedure Register (Routes : in out Router) is
   begin
      Add (Routes, Get, "/todos", List'Access);
      Add (Routes, Post, "/todos", Add_Todo'Access);
   end Register;

end Todo_Store;
```

```ada
Servers.Run (Servers.From_Environment, Routes, Hooks => Todo_Store.Hooks);
```

## PostgreSQL

Needs `sparrow_postgres`. Statements are prepared once per connection; parameters are typed and sent in binary.

```ada
--  user_queries.ads
with Sparrow.Postgres; use Sparrow.Postgres;

package User_Queries is
   procedure Open (Db : in out Connection; Url : String);
   procedure Print_User (Db : in out Connection; Email : String);
end User_Queries;

--  user_queries.adb
with Ada.Text_IO;
with Sparrow; use Sparrow;
with Sparrow.Migrations;
with Sparrow.Postgres.Migrations;
with Sparrow.Postgres.Queries; use Sparrow.Postgres.Queries;

package body User_Queries is

   Steps : constant Sparrow.Migrations.Step_List :=
     [Sparrow.Migrations.Step
        (1, "CREATE TABLE users (id bigserial PRIMARY KEY,"
            & " email text UNIQUE, name text)")];

   Find_User : aliased constant Statement :=
     Define ("find_user", "SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE email = $1");

   --  Url: "postgresql://app@localhost/app"; add "?sslmode=verify-full"
   --  for a server on another machine.
   procedure Open (Db : in out Connection; Url : String) is
   begin
      Connect (Db, Url);
      Postgres.Migrations.Apply (Db, Steps);
      Prepare (Db, Find_User);   --  once per connection
   end Open;

   procedure Print_User (Db : in out Connection; Email : String) is
      Result : Statement_Result;
   begin
      Query (Db, Find_User, [+UTF8_String (Email)], Result);
      for Row in Rows (Db, Result) loop
         Ada.Text_IO.Put_Line
           (Row.Integer_Value ("id")'Image & " " & String (Row.Text ("name")));
      end loop;
   end Print_User;

end User_Queries;
```

In a server, keep one connection per worker: an `array (Worker_Id) of access Connection` filled by the
`On_Start` worker hook, as `examples/notes_api` does.

## Templates

Needs `sparrow_templates`. Mustache: `{{name}}` escaped, `{{{name}}}` raw, `{{#list}}...{{/list}}`.

```html
<!-- templates/articles.mustache -->
<h1>{{title}}</h1>
<ul>{{#articles}}<li>{{title}}</li>{{/articles}}</ul>
```

```ada
--  article_pages.ads
with Sparrow.Http.Routers; use Sparrow.Http.Routers;

package Article_Pages is
   procedure Load_Views;   --  once, at start
   procedure Register (Routes : in out Router);
end Article_Pages;

--  article_pages.adb
with Sparrow; use Sparrow;
with Sparrow.Http; use Sparrow.Http;
with Sparrow.Http.Responses;
with Sparrow.Templates; use Sparrow.Templates;
with Sparrow.Templates.Bindings; use Sparrow.Templates.Bindings;

package body Article_Pages is

   Views : Library;

   procedure Load_Views is
      Loaded, Failed : Natural;
   begin
      --  Every *.mustache file, named by its file name.
      Load_Directory (Views, "templates", Loaded, Failed);
      if Failed > 0 then
         raise Program_Error with "a template does not parse";
      end if;
   end Load_Views;

   procedure Index
     (Request : Http_Request; Response : in out Http_Response)
   is
      pragma Unreferenced (Request);
      Data  : Binding_Set;   --  frees itself
      Found : Boolean;

      procedure Add_Article (Title : UTF8_String) is
         Row : constant Scope := Add_Item (Data, "articles");
      begin
         Set (Data, "title", Title, Within => Row);
      end Add_Article;
   begin
      Set (Data, "title", "Articles");
      Add_Article ("Hello, Ada");   --  in real life, a loop over your rows
      Add_Article ("Sparrow 0.1");
      Responses.Begin_Content (Response, OK, Text_Html);
      Render (Views, "articles", Data, Response.Content, Found);
   end Index;

   procedure Register (Routes : in out Router) is
   begin
      Add (Routes, Get, "/articles", Index'Access);
   end Register;

end Article_Pages;
```

`Sparrow.Templates.Bindings.Add_Rows` turns an SQLite statement's rows into a list in one call, and
`Sparrow.Templates.Json_Data` renders straight from a JSON document.

## Server-Sent Events

Needs `sparrow_http`. One response that stays open; the server pushes events to it from any task.

```ada
--  price_feed.ads
with Sparrow.Http.Routers; use Sparrow.Http.Routers;

package Price_Feed is
   procedure Register (Routes : in out Router);
   procedure Publish (Price : Integer);   --  from any task
end Price_Feed;

--  price_feed.adb
with Sparrow; use Sparrow;
with Sparrow.Http; use Sparrow.Http;
with Sparrow.Http.Event_Streams;
with Sparrow.Http.Requests;
with Sparrow.Http.Streams;

package body Price_Feed is

   Watchers : Streams.Group (Capacity => 10_000);

   --  GET /prices. In the browser:
   --    new EventSource("/prices").addEventListener("price", ...)
   procedure Subscribe
     (Request : Http_Request; Response : in out Http_Response)
   is
   begin
      Event_Streams.Begin_Events (Response);
      Streams.Add (Watchers, Requests.Connection (Request));
   end Subscribe;

   procedure Publish (Price : Integer) is
      Data : constant UTF8_String :=
        "{""price"":" & UTF8_String (Price'Image) & "}";
   begin
      Event_Streams.Send (Watchers, Data, Name => "price");
   end Publish;

   procedure Register (Routes : in out Router) is
   begin
      Add (Routes, Get, "/prices", Subscribe'Access, Run => On_Reactor);
   end Register;

end Price_Feed;
```

Closed connections drop out of the group by themselves; a client that falls too far behind is disconnected.

## WebSockets

Needs `sparrow_http`. A chat room: every message goes to everyone connected.

```ada
--  chat.ads
with Sparrow.Http.Routers; use Sparrow.Http.Routers;

package Chat is
   procedure Register (Routes : in out Router);
end Chat;

--  chat.adb
with Sparrow; use Sparrow;
with Sparrow.Http; use Sparrow.Http;
with Sparrow.Http.Streams;
with Sparrow.Http.Websockets;

package body Chat is

   Everyone : Streams.Group (Capacity => 1_000);

   type Room is new Websockets.Endpoint with null record;

   overriding procedure On_Open
     (This : Room; Socket : Connection_Id; Request : Http_Request);
   overriding procedure On_Message
     (This    : Room;
      Socket  : Connection_Id;
      Message : String;
      Binary  : Boolean;
      Context : Handler_Context);
   overriding procedure On_Close (This : Room; Socket : Connection_Id);

   overriding procedure On_Open
     (This : Room; Socket : Connection_Id; Request : Http_Request) is
   begin
      Streams.Add (Everyone, Socket);
   end On_Open;

   overriding procedure On_Message
     (This    : Room;
      Socket  : Connection_Id;
      Message : String;
      Binary  : Boolean;
      Context : Handler_Context) is
   begin
      if not Binary then
         --  The server has checked that a text message is UTF-8.
         Streams.Send (Everyone, UTF8_String (Message));
      end if;
   end On_Message;

   overriding procedure On_Close (This : Room; Socket : Connection_Id) is
   begin
      Streams.Remove (Everyone, Socket);
   end On_Close;

   procedure Register (Routes : in out Router) is
   begin
      --  In the browser: new WebSocket("ws://localhost:8080/chat")
      Add (Routes, Get, "/chat", Websockets.Serve (new Room));
   end Register;

end Chat;
```

Only pages from the same host may connect; `Serve (..., Allowed_Origins => "https://app.example")` allows others.

## File uploads

Needs `sparrow_http`. A `multipart/form-data` form, held in memory up to the body limit (1 MiB by default).

```ada
--  avatars.ads
with Sparrow.Http.Routers; use Sparrow.Http.Routers;

package Avatars is
   procedure Register (Routes : in out Router);
end Avatars;

--  avatars.adb
with Sparrow.Http; use Sparrow.Http;
with Sparrow.Http.Multipart; use Sparrow.Http.Multipart;
with Sparrow.Http.Responses;

package body Avatars is

   --  <form method=post enctype=multipart/form-data>
   --    <input name=user> <input type=file name=avatar>
   procedure Upload
     (Request : Http_Request; Response : in out Http_Response)
   is
      Fields : Form;
      Valid  : Boolean;
   begin
      Parse (Request, Fields, Valid);
      if not Valid or else not Has_File (Fields, "avatar") then
         Responses.Fail (Response, Bad_Request);
         return;
      end if;
      --  Choose the path yourself: never trust the client's file name.
      Save (Fields, "avatar",
            "uploads/" & String (Field (Fields, "user")) & ".png");
      Responses.Send (Response, Created, "saved");
   end Upload;

   procedure Register (Routes : in out Router) is
   begin
      Add (Routes, Post, "/avatar", Upload'Access);
   end Register;

end Avatars;
```

For files of any size, add the route with `Body_Mode => Streamed` and use `Multipart.Save_Stream`, which
writes each file to disk as it arrives (see `examples/file_drop`).

## Rate limits and CORS

Needs `sparrow_http`.

```ada
--  guarded.ads
with Sparrow.Http.Routers; use Sparrow.Http.Routers;

package Guarded is
   procedure Register (Routes : in out Router);
end Guarded;

--  guarded.adb
with Sparrow.Http; use Sparrow.Http;
with Sparrow.Http.Cors;
with Sparrow.Http.Limits;
with Sparrow.Http.Responses;

package body Guarded is

   --  Per client address: 5 at once, then one every 5 seconds.
   --  Past that, the route answers 429 with Retry-After.
   Logins : constant Limits.Limit :=
     Limits.Per_Client (Rate => 0.2, Burst => 5);

   --  Pages on https://app.example may call /api/... from the browser.
   Api : constant Cors.Policy := Cors.Allow ("https://app.example");

   procedure Log_In
     (Request : Http_Request; Response : in out Http_Response)
   is
      pragma Unreferenced (Request);
   begin
      Responses.Send (Response, OK, "welcome");
   end Log_In;

   procedure Items
     (Request : Http_Request; Response : in out Http_Response)
   is
      pragma Unreferenced (Request);
   begin
      Responses.Send (Response, OK, "[]", Media_Type => Application_Json);
   end Items;

   procedure Register (Routes : in out Router) is
   begin
      Add (Routes, Post, "/login", Limits.Wrap (Logins, Log_In'Access));
      Add (Routes, Options, "/api/*rest", Cors.Preflight (Api),
           Run => On_Reactor);
      Add (Routes, Get, "/api/items", Cors.Share (Api, Items'Access));
   end Register;

end Guarded;
```

Behind a proxy, set `BEHIND_PROXY=on` so the client is read from `X-Forwarded-For`. For limits counted
across several servers, see the Valkey snippet.

## Logs, metrics and health checks

Needs `sparrow_http`. Every request is already logged (one access-log line, with its request id), counted and
timed; this adds your own.

```ada
--  shop.ads
with Sparrow.Http.Routers; use Sparrow.Http.Routers;

package Shop is
   procedure Register (Routes : in out Router);
end Shop;

--  shop.adb
with Sparrow.Http; use Sparrow.Http;
with Sparrow.Http.Health;
with Sparrow.Http.Log;
with Sparrow.Http.Requests;
with Sparrow.Http.Responses;
with Sparrow.Metrics;

package body Shop is

   Orders : constant Sparrow.Metrics.Counter :=
     Sparrow.Metrics.New_Counter ("shop_orders_total", "Orders placed.");

   --  /readyz: whether this instance can serve. Ask your database here.
   function Database_Ready (Request : Http_Request) return Boolean is
      pragma Unreferenced (Request);
   begin
      return True;
   end Database_Ready;

   procedure Order
     (Request : Http_Request; Response : in out Http_Response)
   is
      Item : constant String := Requests.Form_Value (Request, "item");
   begin
      Sparrow.Metrics.Add (Orders);
      --  The line carries the request's id, like its access-log line.
      Log.Info (Request, "order placed", Log.Field ("item", Item));
      Responses.Send (Response, Created, "ordered");
   end Order;

   procedure Register (Routes : in out Router) is
   begin
      Add (Routes, Post, "/orders", Order'Access);
      --  /healthz, /readyz, and /metrics for Prometheus
      Health.Add (Routes, Check => Database_Ready'Access);
   end Register;

end Shop;
```

`LOG_FORMAT=json` writes JSON lines for log collectors. Outside a request, use `Sparrow.Logs.Info (...)`.
Keep `/metrics` off the public side of a load balancer.

## Calling other services

Needs `sparrow_client`.

```ada
--  weather.ads
with Sparrow.Http.Routers; use Sparrow.Http.Routers;

package Weather is
   function Forecast (Request : Http_Request; City : String) return String;
end Weather;

--  weather.adb
with Sparrow.Client; use Sparrow.Client;
with Sparrow.Http.Log;

package body Weather is

   function Forecast (Request : Http_Request; City : String) return String
   is
      Url    : constant String :=
        "https://weather.example/v1/forecast?city=" & Url_Encode (City);
      Answer : Sparrow.Client.Response;
   begin
      --  Trace_Headers carries the request's trace on to the other service.
      Get (Url, Answer,
           Headers => "Accept: application/json" & ASCII.LF
                      & Sparrow.Http.Log.Trace_Headers (Request));
      if Status (Answer) /= 200 then
         return "";
      end if;
      return Content (Answer);
   end Forecast;

end Weather;
```

`Sparrow.Client.Post (Url, Content, Answer, Media_Type => ...)` sends a body. Calls block: make them from
handlers on workers.

## S3 object storage

Needs `sparrow_s3`. Works with AWS and with compatible stores (MinIO, R2, Garage, ...).

```ada
--  photos.ads
with Sparrow.Http.Routers; use Sparrow.Http.Routers;

package Photos is
   procedure Register (Routes : in out Router);
end Photos;

--  photos.adb
with Sparrow.Http; use Sparrow.Http;
with Sparrow.Http.Requests; use Sparrow.Http.Requests;
with Sparrow.Http.Responses;
with Sparrow.S3;

package body Photos is

   --  AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY and AWS_REGION; also
   --  AWS_ENDPOINT_URL for a store other than AWS.
   Bucket : constant Sparrow.S3.Bucket :=
     Sparrow.S3.Bucket_From_Environment ("photos");

   function Key_Of (Request : Http_Request) return String is
     ("photos/" & Parameter (Request, "name"));

   --  PUT /photos/:name with the image as the body
   procedure Store
     (Request : Http_Request; Response : in out Http_Response) is
   begin
      Sparrow.S3.Put (Bucket, Key_Of (Request), Content (Request),
                      Media_Type => "image/jpeg");
      Responses.Send (Response, Created, "stored");
   end Store;

   --  GET /photos/:name: the browser downloads from the store directly,
   --  with a link good for five minutes.
   procedure Fetch
     (Request : Http_Request; Response : in out Http_Response) is
   begin
      Responses.Redirect
        (Response,
         Sparrow.S3.Presigned_Get (Bucket, Key_Of (Request), Lifetime => 300));
   end Fetch;

   procedure Register (Routes : in out Router) is
   begin
      Add (Routes, Put, "/photos/:name", Store'Access);
      Add (Routes, Get, "/photos/:name", Fetch'Access);
   end Register;

end Photos;
```

`S3.Presigned_Put` lets the browser upload straight to the store, so large files never pass through the server.

## Valkey: a cache, and sessions shared by several servers

Needs `sparrow_valkey`. Speaks to Valkey or Redis; no C library.

```ada
--  shared_state.ads
with Sparrow.Http.Limits;
with Sparrow.Http.Sessions;
with Sparrow.IO.Process;
with Sparrow.Valkey.Limits;
with Sparrow.Valkey.Sessions;

package Shared_State is

   Url : constant String :=
     Sparrow.IO.Process.Environment
       ("VALKEY_URL", Default => "valkey://localhost:6379");

   --  Sessions kept in Valkey: every server behind the load balancer sees
   --  them, and they outlive restarts.
   Visitors : constant Sparrow.Http.Sessions.Store :=
     Sparrow.Http.Sessions.Table_Store (Sparrow.Valkey.Sessions.Table (Url));

   --  A rate limit that every server counts together.
   Logins : constant Sparrow.Http.Limits.Limit :=
     Sparrow.Http.Limits.Per_Client
       (0.2, 5, Store => Sparrow.Valkey.Limits.Buckets (Url, "logins"));

   --  Valkey as a cache, over a connection of your own (one per task).
   procedure Cache_Example;

end Shared_State;

--  shared_state.adb
with Sparrow.Logs;

package body Shared_State is

   procedure Cache_Example is
      Cache : Sparrow.Valkey.Connection;
      Hits  : Long_Long_Integer;
   begin
      Sparrow.Valkey.Connect (Cache, Sparrow.Valkey.Server_At (Url));
      Sparrow.Valkey.Set (Cache, "page:/", "<h1>Hello</h1>", Lifetime => 60);
      if Sparrow.Valkey.Get (Cache, "page:/", Default => "") /= "" then
         Hits := Sparrow.Valkey.Increment (Cache, "hits");
         Sparrow.Logs.Info ("cache hit", Sparrow.Logs.Field ("hits", Hits));
      end if;
   end Cache_Example;

end Shared_State;
```

## Tracing with OpenTelemetry

Needs `sparrow_open_telemetry`. Each request becomes a span; spans go to an OpenTelemetry collector over OTLP.

```ada
--  traced_hello.adb
with Greetings;
with Sparrow.Http; use Sparrow.Http;
with Sparrow.Http.Routers; use Sparrow.Http.Routers;
with Sparrow.Http.Servers;
with Sparrow.Open_Telemetry;

procedure Traced_Hello is
   Routes  : Router (Capacity => 8);
   Started : Boolean;
begin
   Greetings.Register (Routes);
   --  On when OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is set (http://localhost:4318).
   Sparrow.Open_Telemetry.Start_From_Environment ("greetings", Started);
   Servers.Run (Servers.From_Environment, Routes);
   Sparrow.Open_Telemetry.Stop;   --  sends what is left
end Traced_Hello;
```

Inside a handler, `Spans.Start (Request, "load user")` adds a span of your own, ended with its block.

## Settings from the environment

`Servers.From_Environment` reads:

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `HOST` | `127.0.0.1` | Address to listen on: `0.0.0.0` for every IPv4 interface, `::` for IPv4 and IPv6 |
| `PORT` | `8080` | Port |
| `REACTORS` | one per processor | Tasks that own the connections |
| `WORKERS` | `8` | Tasks that run handlers which may block |
| `ACCESS_LOG` | `on` | One log line per request |
| `TRUST_TRACE` | `on` | Keep the `X-Request-Id` and `traceparent` a request arrives with; `off` when clients reach the server directly |
| `BEHIND_PROXY` | `off` | Read the client's address from `X-Forwarded-For` (only when every request comes through the proxy) |
| `HTTP_2` | `on` | HTTP/2 by prior knowledge over plain TCP (over TLS, ALPN chooses) |
| `COMPRESSION` | `on` | gzip for responses worth compressing |

Logging (`Sparrow.Logs`) reads `LOG_LEVEL` (`info`) and `LOG_FORMAT` (`text`, or `json` for log collectors).
Or build a `Servers.Configuration` in code and pass it to `Servers.Run`.
